items.prompt: Is kicking a ball a push or a pull?

options.why: A pull brings something towards you. A kick sends the ball away.
A kick makes the ball move, so it is a force.

hints: A push moves something away from you.
Where does the ball go when you kick it?
Picture your foot hitting the ball. Does the ball move away or come closer?
items.explanation: Kicking is a push. Your foot pushes the ball away from you.

items.prompt: Is it a push or a pull? Sort the cards.
hints: A push moves something away. A pull brings it closer.
Act out each one with your hands.
Start with the doorbell. Does your finger move away from you?
items.explanation: Pressing a doorbell, throwing a ball and closing a drawer are pushes. Opening a drawer, taking off a sock and picking a mango are pulls.

items.prompt: Dimas opens a drawer to get a pencil. Is it a push or a pull?

options.why: To open a drawer, you move it towards you.
You do not turn a drawer round to open it.

hints: Watch which way the drawer moves.
Does it come towards you or go away?
Act it out: hold a handle and open it.
items.explanation: Opening a drawer is a pull. The drawer moves towards you.

items.prompt: Pushes and pulls are kinds of ___.
hints: There is one science word for pushes and pulls.
This word is used when something is made to move or stop.
It starts with f and has 5 letters.
items.explanation: Pushes and pulls are forces. A force can make things move, stop or change shape.

items.prompt: Which push will make a toy car go further?

figure.alt: A toy car on the floor.

options.why: A small push makes the car go a short way.
Without a push, the car stays still.

hints: Think about pushing gently and pushing hard.
Which push gives the car more speed?
Picture pushing the car very gently. How far does it go?
items.explanation: A bigger push makes the toy car go faster and further.

items.prompt: Choose all the actions that are pulls.

options.why: Kicking moves the ball away from you, so it is a push.

options.text: taking a book off a shelf

options.why: Pressing moves the key down, away from your finger. It is a push.

hints: A pull brings something towards you.
Act out each one.
Start with the curtain. Which way does your hand move?
items.explanation: Opening a curtain, taking a book off a shelf and tugging a rope are pulls. Kicking and pressing are pushes.

items.prompt: Putu is on a swing. How can his friend make it go higher?

options.why: Pulling the swing down would slow it.
Without pushes, the swing slows down and stops.

hints: Think about what makes a swing move.
Does a harder push or a softer push go higher?
Picture pushing a swing gently, then strongly.
items.explanation: A harder push makes the swing go higher and faster.

items.prompt: Kartika squashes a ball of clay flat. What did her push do?

options.why: The clay stays the same colour.
The clay is still there. It is flat now.

hints: Look at the clay before and after.
What is different about it now?
Compare a round ball with a flat pancake.
items.explanation: A push can change the shape of something. Kartika's push changed the round clay into a flat shape.

items.prompt: A ball is rolling towards you. How can you stop it?

options.why: Shouting cannot push the ball.
Looking does not push or pull the ball.

options.text: push against it with your hand

hints: Forces can stop things moving.
Which choice uses a push or a pull?
Picture catching a rolling ball. What do your hands do?
items.explanation: Pushes and pulls can stop moving things. Putting your hand against the ball pushes on it and stops it.

items.prompt: Two teams play tug of war. Which force do both teams use?

options.why: In tug of war, both teams move the rope towards themselves.
The teams do not turn the rope round.

hints: Think about which way each team moves the rope.
Does each team move the rope towards itself or away?
Act it out with a scarf or a towel.
items.explanation: In tug of war, both teams pull the rope towards themselves. The team with the stronger pull wins.

items.prompt: Which one needs a push and a pull?

options.why: Kicking is only a push.

options.text: opening and then closing a door

options.why: Pressing is only a push.

hints: Look for a choice with two actions.
One action moves something towards you and the other moves it away.
Act out opening a door, then closing it.
items.explanation: Opening and closing a door uses a pull one way and a push the other way.

items.prompt: Ravi pushes his toy car the same way each time. He tries a carpet and a smooth floor. Where does it roll further?

figure.alt: A toy car, a rough carpet and a smooth floor.

options.why: The carpet is rough. It slows the car down more.
The rough carpet slows the car more than the smooth floor.

hints: Think about how the two surfaces feel.
Rough surfaces slow moving things down more than smooth ones.
Picture rolling a ball on a rug and on tiles.
items.explanation: The car rolls further on the smooth floor. The rough carpet rubs against the wheels and slows the car down more.
